page_title: ProcessSpy – The macOS Process Explorer & Advanced Monitor

sources.entry: ProcessSpy - A clean and powerful process monitor.

summary.name: ProcessSpy
summary.one_liner: ProcessSpy is a native macOS process explorer and monitor that shows process trees, command lines, environment variables, and historical CPU/memory data beyond what Activity Monitor offers.
use_cases: Identify which of several same-named processes (e.g., multiple java versions) is running
Investigate CPU or memory spikes over time
Inspect a process's command line, environment variables, and signature
Review how an app's helper and XPC child processes add up
Export process history to CSV for reporting
Search processes by name and command-line arguments with regex
summary.what_it_does: ProcessSpy displays macOS processes with per-process CPU and memory history, CPU QoS breakdown, memory footprint, and real-time disk I/O and memory pressure rates. Its hierarchy view groups child and XPC processes under their responsible PID and shows aggregate CPU, memory, and thread totals. Quick-search supports regular expressions and multiple properties at once, and advanced filters can be written in JavaScript. It keeps finished processes with their command lines, environment variables, and history for later review, and can export history to CSV. A menu bar dashboard provides system health at a glance.
notable: Remembers finished processes with command lines, environment variables, and history
Groups XPC and helper processes by responsible PID with rolled-up totals
Regex and JavaScript-based search and filters
Available via Homebrew cask and on Setapp
caveats: Several features (history, CSV export, deep inspection) are marked as Paid
